The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.07.2022.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 30.07.2022 at about 12.15 p.m., the petitioner was riding his Activa bearing No.KA-40-EF-2691 on the extreme left side of Chikkaballapuara- Bengaluru NH-44 slowly and cautiously, and at that time the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811 drove the same at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly steered towards his extreme left side and stopped without switching on the indicator nor observing the side mirror, in the said process accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital, thereafter shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein petitioner took conservative treatment as an inpatient and further he was shifted to Sri Sai Hospitals, Yadavanahalli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru.
The petitioner has spent an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- towards hospitalization charges, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident,
petitioner was aged about 65 years, hale and healthy and was doing Agriculture and Real Estate Business and earning Rs.36,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to do his work as he was doing prior to the said accident and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The respondent No.2 is the insurer and respondent No. 1 and 3 are the owner and policy holder of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

3. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.1 and 3 have not appeared before the tribunal,
hence respondent No.1 and 3 placed exparte.
After service of summons, respondent No.2-insurer has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
The respondent No.2- insurer has filed written statement by denying the cause and manner of accident.
Further it has denied the issuance of policy to the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.

2

Further it is submitted that after due verification of their records the policy number 0162839260 00 00 was issued by this respondent in respect of Auto secure commercial vehicle package policy for the vehicle bearing Reg. NO.TN-23-CD-6571.
Further this respondent submits that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
It has denied the involvement of the offending lorry in the alleged accident.
Further it has also denied the age, occupation, income and injuries sustained by the petitioner and also the treatment taken for the injuries.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievious injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg.No.NL-01-AF-6811 by its driver, in RTA took place on 30.07.2022 at about 12.15 p.m on Chikkaballapur-Bengaluru NH-44 road, near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Chikkaballapura?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what amount & from whom?
3.
What order or award?
5. In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner himself is examined as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 15.
Further petitioner has also examined two witnesses as PW2 and 3 and got marked documents at Ex.P16 to P.22.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW1 and got marked one document at Ex.R.1.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 :

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final orders

for the following:-
 : R E A S O N S:
 ISSUE NO.1 :
8.
That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner filed affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, seizure mahazar, sketch, IMV report, charge sheet, wound certificate, Discharge summaries, IMV notice and reply, and all these documents are marked under Ex.P.1 to P.10.
Srirama M vs Vijayalakshmi.M on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80715091/
3 9.

On perusal of Ex.P1- FIR is registered on the basis of first information given by one Smt.
Rathnamma who is the wife of the petitioner by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL- 01-AF-6811.
After the registration of FIR as per Ex.P1, the Ex.P3 spot mahazar and Ex.P4 spot sketch was drawn.
On perusal of Ex.P4 spot sketch, the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road.
10. The Ex.P5 is the IMV report wherein the motorcycle of the petitioner has got damages in its head light, frond side body.
On the other hand the offending Lorry bearing No. NL-01-AF-6811 has got damages in its rear right side brake light, rear right side indicator.
The contents of Ex.P3, 4 and 5 supported the case of the petitioner to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.
If the driver of Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811 driven the same without changing lane toward left side and stopped his vehicle abruptly this accident was not going to be caused.
The respondent No.1 and 3 being the owner not examined his driver by denying the negligence of the driver of the lorry.

11. Ex.P6 charge sheet is also came to be filed on against the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF- 6811, and the IO has opined that the negligence is on the part of driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.
No other grounds are made out by the respondents to show the contributory negligence from the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.1 and 3 -owner neither appeared nor produced any document in support of their case.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has filed written statement and also examined its official who is an official witness by denying the negligence and their liability but not produced any documents in support of its case.
The evidence of RW.1 is based on the documents as he is not witness to the accident.
The document which are produced before this Tribunal establishes the negligence of the driver of the lorry.
As discussed supra, the petitioner successfully established the actionable negligence by the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.

Thus, by considering all these points this court is of the opinion that the said accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.
13.
The alleged accident is of dated 30.07.2022 but the FIR was registered on 01.08.2022 i.e., after 1 day of accident.

In this regard petitioner summoned and produced Ex.P17 & 18 MLC and Police intimation and Ex.P.8 discharge summaries where it evidentiates that on 31.07.2022 itself the petitioner admitted to Sri Sai hospital with a history RTA hit and run by a lorry while petitioner was driving his 2 wheeler.
As per Ex.P.17 and P.18 MLC and police intimation also mentioned same in discharge summaries.
Thus as per Ex.P.2 the petitioner assigned reasons for delay in lodging the complaint that the petitioner was under treatment.
Thereby the delay of 1 day in filing the complaint is explained by the petitioner by producing these documents.
14. The first respondent who is the owner of the offending vehicle does not chosen to deny the allegation of the rash and negligence driving.
The charge sheet is came to be filed on the the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

At this juncture, I would like to quote the following judgment wherein it states that;

4 2009 ACJ 287 ( National Ins. Co. V/s.
Pushparama and others), wherein it is held that, Certified copy of the criminal court records such as FIR, recovery and mechanical inspection of the vehicle or documents are of sufficient proof to reach the conclusion that the rider was negligent.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

15. In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

sentences.text: Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, wherein it is held that, it was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

16. In support of these documentary evidence, if we perused the oral evidence of the petitioner on this point, even though the respondent no.2 made a suggestions to the petitioner by denying their liability and alleged negligence, nothing being elicited or produced to probabalise the said defence.
17. The contents of Ex.P3 and 4 spot mahazar and spot sketch, Ex.P5 IMV report helped the petitioner to prove his case.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 10 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.
18. As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 30.07.2022 which was caused by the driver of the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811 which belonging to respondent No.1 and 3.
There is no reason to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary, but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
19.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

Srirama M vs Vijayalakshmi.M on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80715091/
5 20.
The petitioner has produced wound certificate as per Ex.P7 which shows that the petitioner sustained deep lacerated over right side of fronto parietal area, right frontal depressed fracture.
Without examining the disability by the doctor, it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained permanent disability due to grievous injuries.
21. According to the petitioner he was doing Agriculture and Real Estate business and earning Rs.36,000/- p.m.
But to prove his avocation and income, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

22. While determining the compensation this court has to look into the pain and sufferings, medical expenses, diet, food, nourishment, attendant and conveyance charges and loss of amenities and enjoyment of life that the PW-1 has suffered, which are discussed herein below:
(A) TOWARDS PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
The petitioner has relied upon Ex.P.7 - wound certificate and Ex.P8 discharge summaries, which make it crystal clear that PW-1 has sustained grievous injury.
The petitioner was admitted to NIMHANS Hospital on 30.07.2022 and discharged on 31.07.2022 and admitted to Sri Sai Hospitals from 31.07.2022 to 08.08.2022.

Hence keeping in mind the injuries mentioned in wound certificate, it can be said that the petitioner must have undergone some amount of physical pain and sufferings, for which, an amount of Rs.
40,000/- can be held to be just and proper compensation under this head.
(B) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced medical bills which is marked as Ex.P-12 amounting to Rs.1,26,653/-.
These bills are supported with the prescriptions marked at Ex.P13.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitled for the reimbursement of the bills by rounding off the same i.e., Rs.1,26,700/- is awarded under this head.
(C) TOWARDS DIET, FOOD, NOURISHMENT, ATTENDANT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
As already observed the discharge summary Ex.P-8, makes it amply clear that the petitioner underwent conservative treatment for the injuries sustained by him.
During the said period the petitioner might have taken assistance from others and taken diet food.
On consideration of the injuries sustained by the petitioner this Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and proper to award an amount of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

(D) TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNING CAPACITY ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
Srirama M vs Vijayalakshmi.

M on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80715091/
6
It is necessary to note that the loss of future earning capacity cannot be presumed and has to be proved with cogent evidence.

But interestingly the petitioner though claims that he is unable to do any work and has become permanently disabled he has not put in any efforts to prove the disability by examining the doctor, who treated him.
In fact he has not even produced the disability certificate issued by competent authority.
In the absence of any such material piece of evidence, it is very difficult for this Court to assess the disability and thereby assess the loss of earning capacity due to disability.

Hence, this court has no option but to hold that the petitioner has not suffered any permanent physical disability which has resulted in reduction of his income and hence he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
(E) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:

The petitioner has not made out any evidence or grounds to hold that he sustained the loss of income during the laid down period hence, in the absence of any evidence,
petitioner is not entitled for any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
(F) TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES AND ENJOYMENT OF LIFE:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award him a reasonable sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.
(G) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES: NIL 23.

To sum up the above discussion, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following A) Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/- B) Towards Medical expenses Rs.1,26,700/- C)
Towards diet, food, nourishment, Rs. 20,000/-
 attendant and conveyance charges D) Towards loss of future earning Nil  capacity E) Loss of income during laid up Nil  period F) Towards loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-

24. Liability:-
The respondent No.2- insurer has filed written statement by denying the issuance of policy to the Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.
But submitted that the policy number 0162839260 00 00 was issued by this respondent in respect of Auto secure commercial vehicle package policy for the vehicle bearing Reg. NO.TN- 23-CD-6571.
In this regard the offending vehicle before this Tribunal is lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811.
The petitioner summoned the PW.3 who was the GPA holder of the said Lorry bearing No.NL-01-AF-6811 who produced the notarized copy of certificate of registration of Government of Nagaland as Ex.P21.
The said Ex.P21 marked subject to objection as the original was not produced by the PW.3.
But the Ex.P21 is the notarized copy.
On perusal of Ex.P21 the vehicle No.TN-23-CD- 6571 was registered and renumbered in the Nagaland government RTO as NL-01-AF-6811.
The said registration was done with new number before RTO of Nagaland on 12.04.2022.
The accident in question before this Tribunal was on 30.07.2022.
Thereby there was valid policy for vehicle bearing No. TN-23-CD-6571 as on the date of the accident as admitted by the respondent No.2.
Nearly because of the sale of the vehicle and registering with new number before the another RTO will not vitiates the policy.
25. No other grounds are made out by showing the contributory negligence of the petitioner or violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.1 and 3 owner and policy holder.
Hence the Respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the liability of respondent No.1- and 3.
The petitioner is entitled for the interest @ 6% p.a.
Accordingly, this issue answered in the affirmative.
26. ISSUE NO.3:
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER The petition filed by the petitioner U/s. 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,11,700/- (Rupees Two lakhs eleven thousand seven hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 - insurance  company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
